## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

behavior nobody reviews. Report what you found either way.

2	//
3	// A pack is activated by matching the id a member DECLARED against the id a pack
4	// module carries, literally. So the moment a canon pack's directory is renamed, every
5	// member's declaration is one cycle stale by construction, and a member holding the
6	// old spelling beside the new mount does not get a degraded pack — it gets NO pack,
7	// because nothing matches. For a pack carrying the `update` task that is terminal:
8	// the member loses the machinery that would have delivered its own repair, and the
9	// only route back in is a hand-run against each repo (#1004 is this failure with a
10	// smaller blast radius).
11	//
12	// The declaration rewrite still happens — the migration record converges every
13	// member onto today's spelling, so this map is a tolerance and not the mechanism.
14	// What the map buys is that no ORDERING of the two halves can strand anyone: a
15	// member reads correctly whether its declaration has been rewritten yet or not, and
16	// whether its mount is ahead of its declaration or behind it.
17	//
18	// STRAIGHT TO TODAY'S, never chained. A second rename of an already-renamed pack
19	// adds its oldest spelling here pointing at the newest name, so a declaration
20	// written for the very first vocabulary still normalizes in ONE pass — a chain of
21	// one-step hops would need as many passes as there have been renames, and every
22	// caller would have to know to loop.
23	//
24	// RETIREMENT is read off the fleet, never off a calendar: an entry comes out when
25	// no member's declaration and no member's stamped `packVersions` still carries that
26	// spelling. Until then it is load-bearing for exactly the repos that have not
27	// converged, which are the repos least able to complain.
28	export const RENAMED_PACKS = Object.freeze({
29	  core: 'claudinite-lifecycle',
30	  grow_with_claudinite: 'claudinite-growth',
31	});
32	
33	// The canon id a spelling resolves to. Canon packs only — a LOCAL pack lives in the
34	// member's own tree and its id is that repo's to choose, so a local pack that happens
35	// to be called `core` is a different pack than the canon one and must not be renamed
36	// out from under its owner.
37	export const canonicalPackId = (id) => RENAMED_PACKS[id] ?? id;
38	
39	// The same map over the keys of a stamp's `packVersions`. A renamed pack whose
40	// stamped version still sits under the old key reads as version-ABSENT, which is not
41	// a harmless miss: absent means "never installed", so the install flow claims it,
42	// stamps it at latest, and runs NO migration records — silently skipping every record
43	// in the gap the update flow would have applied.
44	export function canonicalPackVersions(packVersions) {
45	  if (!packVersions || typeof packVersions !== 'object') return packVersions;
46	  const out = {};
47	  for (const [id, version] of Object.entries(packVersions)) {
48	    const to = canonicalPackId(id);
49	    // A declaration mid-converge can carry BOTH spellings. Today's wins: it is the
50	    // one the flows have written, and the legacy key is the residue they replace.
51	    if (to !== id && Object.hasOwn(packVersions, to)) continue;
52	    out[to] = version;
53	  }
54	  return out;
55	}
